questions.q: What does this card show over 13 months? AC-4 asks for a batched 13-month series sharing DEV-2467's cache key, but that key covers ONE window and the 13-month buckets are namespaced to UniqueScanCounts and unreadable from here (S10). Three options: (A) sparkline = the org-total monthly trend, sharing a NEW class-neutral monthly key added to ScanPlateStatsBatchQuery and read by both cards -- zero extra scans, small lockstep change to DEV-2467's card; (B) no 13-month surface at all -- the card shows only the selected window's ranking; (C) a full 13-month x per-kit stacked chart matching the RecoveryLeader visual -- requires the combined GROUP BY month, kit_id shape that DEV-2466 never measured and ScanPlateStatsBatchQuery::handle()'s docblock forbids adding without a fresh measurement.
questions.answer: OPTION A. The 13 bars are the ORG-TOTAL monthly distinct-plate trend, served from a NEW class-neutral monthly cache key added to ScanPlateStatsBatchQuery (mirroring sharedRangeCacheKey()), read by BOTH this card and UniqueScanCounts. The ranked kit list covers the SELECTED WINDOW only. Zero new ClickHouse scans. Option C (13-month x per-kit stacked chart) was REJECTED on two grounds, both put to the operator: (1) it needs the combined GROUP BY month, kit_id shape that has never been measured, and Q2 established that measurement is not currently obtainable; (2) a stacked bar visually implies its segments sum to the bar total, but per-kit distinct plates do NOT sum to the org distinct total (a plate seen by two kits counts in both) -- so C would ship a chart that overstates the real total. RecoveryLeader may stack safely only because its per-kit values are fractional attribution SHARES that genuinely do sum. This makes the shipped shape identical in spirit to StagingLiveHitLeader: sparkline = the shared org series, ranked list = this card's own leaderboard, and the two are never conflated.

questions.q: The DEV-2466 envelope did not reproduce today. Running DEV-2467's ALREADY-SHIPPED 13-month org-total query for org 469 against production ClickHouse Cloud as readonly_user hit a 20,000 ms SERVER-SIDE execution cap and was killed, against DEV-2466's recorded 1,102 ms. A single-month org-total on the same org returned in ~2,290 ms wall. This is not attributable to this ticket's code -- it is the shipped sibling's query -- and it may be cluster contention or a replica/settings difference rather than a real regression (DEV-2464's lesson: sequential ClickHouse benchmarks mis-blame contention on query shape). But AC-5 asks this card to stay 'within the DEV-2466 envelope', and that envelope is currently unreproducible. Proceed on DEV-2466's recorded numbers, or re-baseline the envelope first?
questions.answer: RE-BASELINE THE ENVELOPE FIRST. Do not proceed to plan/implement on DEV-2466's recorded numbers. Run a proper INTERLEAVED measurement (never sequential batches -- DEV-2464's lesson is that sequential runs mis-attribute contention spikes to query shape) of the already-shipped shapes against production ClickHouse Cloud, and record the result as this ticket's authoritative envelope. Operator explicitly declined the variant that would also file a defect against DEV-2467; do not create any Jira ticket without asking. || RE-BASELINE COMPLETE (D6/D7/D8): DEV-2466's envelope REPRODUCES -- 13-month org-total 1,056-1,152 ms (recorded 1,102) and single-window rollup 584-676 ms (recorded 606). D4's 20 s kill was NOT query shape and NOT a DEV-2467 regression: it was a COLD-PARTITION first touch (measured 5.7x penalty, 853 ms warm -> 4,861 ms cold) colliding with a standing max_execution_time=20 s on the readonly_user profile. No defect exists against DEV-2467; no Jira ticket filed, per the operator's choice. AC-5 may be judged against the DEV-2466 envelope as originally written.

sharedRangeCacheKey() requires BYTE-IDENTICAL start/end/timezone strings. If this card's arguments differ from UniqueScanCounts' by so much as whitespace or a zone spelling, both cards miss the cache and each issue their own scan -- silently defeating the entire reason this ticket exists. Use static::clarityDb(), never a hardcoded 'clarity.' prefix. Copy HitStatsBatchQuery / HitPlateStatsBatchQuery, not RecoveryLeaderQuery or ScanStatsBatchQuery.

A = org 469 -- the org EVERY prior production measurement (D7/D9/D10) used. B = org 1271 -- the actual worst-case org, identified here. derivation_log.aggregate_result: CARDINALITY (2026-08, all 390 orgs): org 1271 is the worst case on BOTH axes -- 13,795,620 rows and 81 kits. Org 469, the prior baseline, is only 2nd by rows (5,462,693) and 4th by kits (35). No org has higher kit cardinality. TIMING wall ms: A(469) = 793 / 651 / 634; B(1271) = 1168 / 1179 / 1134. SERVER-SIDE (X-ClickHouse-Summary): A = 5,578,453 rows, 236 MB, 36 groups, 0.55 GiB peak memory, 525 ms. B = 13,911,711 rows, 510 MB, 82 groups, 0.96 GiB peak memory, 996-1,361 ms. SCALING: 2.5x rows and 2.3x groups produce only 1.8x wall and 1.75x memory -- SUB-LINEAR.
derivation_log.why: Closes the last open scale question. D7/D9/D10 all measured org 469 and labelled it 'worst-case class', which meant worst-case PARAMETER class (a single org id), NOT the largest org -- so the true worst case had never been measured. VERDICT: the envelope HOLDS. The worst case in production is ~1.15 s wall / 0.96 GiB, which is the same order as the 13-month org-total query that DEV-2467 already ships (1,056-1,152 ms, D7), and roughly 17x under the standing 20 s max_execution_time cap on the readonly_user profile. Sub-linear scaling means kit cardinality is not a latent cliff. RESIDUAL, recorded not fixed: on a COLD partition D8 measured a 5.7x first-touch penalty, which would put this worst case near 6.6 s -- still inside the 20 s cap, but it is the same cold-start effect as the unfixed deploy-time residual the operator declined to file.
